claims: The Artemis II mission concluded with a successful splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Orion spacecraft brought the four-person crew back to Earth.
The four-person crew was recovered by the USS John P. Murtha.
The spacecraft is the Orion capsule named Integrity.
The Artemis II mission duration was 10 days.
The splashdown marked the first time humans returned from the vicinity of the Moon in over 50 years.
The crew completed a "textbook" return after evaluating the spacecraft's systems.
